questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code guards concurrent updates to gold and listings? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two different buyers press Buy on the same active listing in the same instant. Which mechanism ensures only one of them gets the item?
choices: buyer.with_lock, because it serializes the two purchase requests.
The surrounding transaction, because it makes the two requests run one after the other.
The optimistic version check performed by listing.update!, which raises StaleObjectError for the request that loses the race.
The listing.active? guard, because it reads the current database state under a lock.

questions.prompt: A buyer's with_lock block finishes and the code continues to listing.update!. When is the buyer's row lock released?
choices: Only when the outer ApplicationRecord.transaction commits or rolls back, because with_lock joined the transaction that was already open.
At the end of the with_lock block, so the row is free for other requests while the listing is updated.
Immediately after buyer.update! executes, because the UPDATE statement releases row locks.
When the controller action returns, because the lock belongs to the request.

questions.prompt: The same buyer double-clicks and two requests arrive at once for two different listings priced 70 and 60 gold. The buyer has 100 gold. What happens?
choices: Both succeed and the buyer ends with -30 gold, because they do not conflict on a listing.
Both fail with StaleObjectError because the buyer row changed.
Both succeed because each request read 100 gold before the other committed.
One request waits on the buyer row lock, then re-reads the reduced balance (with_lock reloads the record), and raises InsufficientGold.
